key_insight: Deep representation learning is not universally better than PCA for scRNA-seq clustering; its value depends on dataset scale and structure.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical analytics pipelines, the study helps teams choose clustering methods that balance accuracy, compute cost, and tuning effort when interpreting single-cell data.
method: Benchmarked 9 clustering pipelines on 10 real scRNA-seq datasets.
Added a partial scVI V2 comparison on 7 datasets.
Used Optuna tuning, repeated runs, and Friedman/Wilcoxon-Holm/TOST plus Sobol sensitivity analysis.
evidence_signal: Across datasets ranging from 90 to 5,685 cells and 4 to 11 cell types, the contrastive autoencoder had the highest mean ARI (0.7872), but post hoc tests did not show clear dominance over the best baselines.
watch_item: Performance was dataset-dependent, so a model that wins on one scRNA-seq cohort may not generalize without careful tuning and sensitivity checks.
paper_title: When Does Deep Representation Learning Help Single-Cell Clustering? A Sensitivity-Aware Diagnostic Benchmark for Biomedical AI Pipelines
